action: No action needed; for awareness. SAP says it has found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data so far.
date_note: The dpa report gives only its own publication day, 26 November; no earlier day is stated.
exec: SAP confirmed suspicious activity and says it has no evidence so far of unauthorized access to customer business data. Der Spiegel reports source code was targeted.
geo_basis: headquarters: Walldorf, as stated by the source
plain: SAP says it found suspicious activity and has seen no sign so far of unauthorized access to customer business data. Der Spiegel reported hackers got employee tokens and could copy and change source code; SAP has not detailed the intrusion.
summary: SAP confirmed the incident in a statement to Recorded Future News, saying it spotted suspicious activity and found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data so far. Der Spiegel reported that hackers targeted SAP's GitHub development environment and obtained employee authentication tokens that let them copy and modify source code. SAP has not disclosed the nature or extent of the intrusion, according to The Record.
title: SAP confirms suspicious activity; Der Spiegel reports hackers targeted its GitHub environment

validation.note: The Record and dpa (onvista/NWZonline, one report) each report SAP's statement of suspicious activity and no evidence so far of unauthorized access to customer data; Cyber Security News and Business Today relay it too. Der Spiegel's original and SAP's own page were not read; the GitHub token claim is Der Spiegel's, relayed by The Record.

review.note: re-compared SAP statement, Spiegel report, token claim attributed to Spiegel against onvista dpa and Cyber Security News
